subject: Prompt & response retention audit request — sample logs and opt-out confirmation
messages:
From: Jane Enright <jane.enright@finsecure.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 08:14:00 -0500
Subject: Request: sample prompt/response retention logs + opt-out confirmation

Hi Olga,

FinSecure is preparing for a targeted vendor audit focused on AI processing and privacy. Two items we need from Redwood for the audit: 1) evidence of how long customer prompt/response data is retained across hosted and dedicated deployments (policy + a small sample extract with timestamps and field names, redacted as needed) and 2) confirmation of how opt-out requests are implemented (i.e., prompt-level opt-out, account-level opt-out, and whether opt-out blocks use of prompts for any training/quality improvements).

We also need to understand whether anything in the retention pipeline is covered by SCCs or special EU data flows and whether we need a DPA amendment. Target timeline is next week. Please let me know what you can provide and any blockers.

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Enright
Head of Compliance, FinSecure
compliance@finsecure.com
Attachment: finsecure-audit-request-20261201.pdf

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Enright <jane.enright@finsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 10:02:13 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: sample prompt/response retention logs + opt-out confirmation

Hi Jane,

Thanks for the detailed ask and the timeline. We can support this audit — below is the plan I propose:

- Marissa will provide our retention policy and a redacted sample extract (CSV) with anonymized IDs and timestamps.
- Rishi will confirm the technical implementation of opt-out across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and provide notes on in-transit/at-rest protections and SCC applicability.
- If a DPA amendment is needed we can draft one and route it via DocuSign; I’ll include a draft for your review.

Two quick clarifying questions from our side:
1) For sample extracts, what fields can be redacted by you vs. what fields you need present (e.g., session_id, account_id, prompt_text redacted but prompt_length and timestamp required)?
2) Do you require chain-of-custody evidence (audit trail for when data was produced) or just the retention policy + sample?

We’ll aim to send the policy and sample by EOD Friday (your timezone) and flag any items that require a DPA amendment.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Customer Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Enright <jane.enright@finsecure.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 09:28:45 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: sample prompt/response retention logs + opt-out confirmation

Hi Jane,

Attaching our current retention policy and a redacted sample extract as requested. Highlights: 

- Policy: "redwood-data-retention-policy.pdf" (attached) — default retention for prompt/response pairs in Hosted is 90 days; Dedicated customers can opt for shorter windows via contract and Private deployments are controlled by customer-managed retention configs.
- Sample extract: "retention-extract-example.csv" (attached) — we redacted prompt_text and replaced account_id with an anonymized customer_id; timestamps are in UTC and we included a retention_cutoff column showing the scheduled deletion date.
- Training: By default, customer prompts in Hosted are not used to improve open model weights; they are used for service quality improvements (e.g., telemetry and anonymized metrics) unless explicitly opted out via contractual terms. Dedicated and Private customers retain full control — training-only uses require written consent per our DPA.
- SCCs/Data flows: We use EU SCCs for EU customer data when required; export controls and cross-border flow notes are in the attached policy.

Next steps: if you confirm the sample fields are sufficient, we can prepare a short audit memo and provide chain-of-custody logs that show when the extract was produced.

Regards,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-data-retention-policy.pdf; retention-extract-example.csv

From: Jane Enright <jane.enright@finsecure.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 14:11:02 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: sample prompt/response retention logs + opt-out confirmation

Hi Marissa / Olga,

Thanks for the quick turn. The sample extract looks helpful — a couple of follow-ups: 

- Can you confirm whether the sample includes any hashed or pseudonymized prompt content used for model quality analysis? If so, we need to understand the reversible/non-reversible nature.
- We also need a statement on how opt-outs are enforced for accounts that are mid-contract and how opt-out propagates to backups and long-term logs.

If you can provide a short technical memo that explains the redaction/pseudonymization approach and a one-paragraph confirmation on backups and DPA implications, that would be ideal for our audit packet.

Thanks,
Jane

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Enright <jane.enright@finsecure.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2026 16:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: sample prompt/response retention logs + opt-out confirmation

Hi Jane — following up with the technical clarifications you requested. Short answers first, then details: 

- Pseudonymization: We do not store reversible ciphertext of prompt_text in the redaction pipeline for external audit extracts. For quality telemetry we may store one-way hashes and aggregated signals (e.g., prompt_length distribution). Hashing is salt+SHA256 for telemetry; salts are not stored alongside the hash for audit extracts.
- Backups & long-term logs: Our backup retention follows the same policy as the primary data store (retention_cutoff enforced at deletion time). When an opt-out is enacted, we schedule deletion jobs for primary stores and scan backups for matching objects; matched backup objects are queued for deletion as allowed by underlying storage provider policies. For immutable backup media that cannot be modified immediately, we mark records as excluded from processing and document the exception in the audit memo.
- Opt-out enforcement across modes: Hosted: opt-out can be applied at the account level via support ticket + DPA amendment; Dedicated: opt-out is controlled by customer configuration/contract; Private: customer-managed, Redwood does not modify.
- SCCs & data transfers: We apply SCCs where stipulated in contract; our DPA template and proposed amendment make this explicit.

I attached a short draft DPA amendment that adds a training/processing opt-out clause and a small sample CSV extract that mirrors the audit sample (retention-extract-example.csv). If you approve the language we can route the DPA via DocuSign for signatures and include a one-paragraph chain-of-custody memo.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm sample fields are sufficient (account anonymization and timestamps).
2) Approve DPA amendment language or propose edits.
3) We will produce the chain-of-custody memo and coordinate DocuSign.

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachments: retention-extract-example.csv; dpa-amendment-draft.docx
